en: The Ritual Manual for the Contemplative Practice and Offerings to Tathāgata Amitāyus.
Compiled by [Name], Grand Master of the Household with the Rank of Peer of the State, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sui, with a Fief of Three Thousand Households;
invested with purple robes, posthumously granted the rank of Minister of Works, and conferred the posthumous title of "Great Mirror" (Dajian).
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Monastery, of Correct Name and Great Vast Wisdom, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi was present within the great assembly of the Buddha Vairocana.
Rising from his seat, he joined his palms in reverence and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One."
For the sake of sentient beings of evil karma in the future world of defilement during the age of the Dharma’s decay,
I shall expound the *Amida Buddha Dhāraṇī*.
By practicing the three gates of mystery, they shall realize the Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha, attain rebirth in the Pure Land, and enter the stage of the Bodhisattva’s correct position.
One cannot be born in that land through meager merit or without wisdom and skillful means. Therefore,
by relying on these teachings and practicing with right mindfulness,
one will certainly be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the highest of the high grades.
One attains the first bhūmi.
If there are those, whether lay or ordained, who wish to be reborn in a pure land,
they should first enter a maṇḍala and receive empowerment.
Thereafter, one should receive from the master the ritual procedures for recitation (*japa*).
Whether at an excellent location or wherever one dwells,
one should cleanse and smear the ground to purify it, and establish a square mandala.
Above, a celestial canopy is spread, with banners suspended all around.
Upon the altar, eight maṇḍalas are distributed;
white sandalwood paste is ground and used to smear the sacred seats.
Place an image of Amitāyus on the western side of the maṇḍala.
The reciter sits on the eastern side of the maṇḍala,
facing west toward the image.
One may spread out mats of *kuśa* grass or sit upon low-legged stools or small couches.
Three times each day, one scatters various kinds of flowers, burns various kinds of incense, and places two *kaṭhaka* [vessels].
Alternatively, one may use basins, cups, or vessels made of gold, silver, copper, stone, porcelain, or earthenware that have not yet been used.
Fill a vessel with scented water and place it upon the altar.
At the four corners of the altar, set four auspicious vases (kalaśa).
Burn incense, light lamps, and offer fragrant ointments, food, and drink according to one's means.
One should perform each consecration with earnest and respectful offerings.
The practitioner should bathe every day and wear fresh, clean garments;
alternatively, one may use mantras to empower the water for bathing.
He then reflected and observed that all sentient beings are pure by nature,
yet are obscured by adventitious defilements.
Failing to awaken to the True Principle,
they lose their way on the path to Bodhi and sink into the cycle of birth and death.
They undergo immeasurable suffering;
therefore, these three secret empowerments are taught so that both oneself and others may attain purification.
Then, with both hands joined in the lotus-anjali gesture,
recite the mantra for purifying the three karmas three times.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ svabhāvaśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvaśuddho ’haṃ. By the empowerment of this mantra, [so it is].
This constitutes the purification of the inner mind through bathing.
Whenever entering the maṇḍala,
one should stand with the body upright and straight, facing the deity.
With palms joined like a lotus and eyes closed,
direct the mind toward the Land of Ultimate Bliss,
visualizing yourself before the Tathāgata Amitāyus together with his retinue of bodhisattvas.
Then, prostrating with the five limbs of the body touching the ground,
one should visualize oneself respectfully paying homage before each and every Buddha and Bodhisattva,
and recite the Mantra of Universal Prostration as follows:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatapraṇāmam akārṣam. (Then, place the right knee on the ground and join the palms at the heart.)
With sincere devotion, one confesses and repents all karmic obstructions and transgressions committed since beginningless time;
then, one rejoices in all the meritorious deeds cultivated by the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and all sentient beings.
Furthermore, they observe all Tathāgatas throughout the worlds of the ten directions who have attained equal and perfect enlightenment,
entreating them to turn the wheel of Dharma;
and all Tathāgatas who are manifesting parinirvāṇa.
Please remain long in this world and do not pass into parinirvāṇa.
Furthermore, he made this vow:
"That which I have accumulated..."
Having paid homage to the Buddhas, repented, rejoiced in merit, and made requests for their teaching,
I dedicate this immeasurable root of goodness and this accumulation of merit to all sentient beings.
May they all be reborn in the world of Ultimate Bliss.
Upon seeing the Buddha and hearing the Dharma, they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Thereafter, they shall sit in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka) or the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka),
with the right leg placed over the left.
Anointing the hands with incense,
first form the Samaya-mudrā of the Buddha Family by joining the two hands with palms hollowed together.
Spread the two index fingers slightly bent,
each resting upon the upper joint of the middle finger;
then, spread the two thumbs.
Twist each ring finger down upon the first joint.
Once the mudrā has been formed,
visualize the Tathāgata Amitāyus with his thirty-two major marks and eighty minor signs, appearing with perfect clarity.
Then, recite the Samaya-mantra of the Buddha Family as follows:
Oṃ tathāgatādya-nābhāya svāhā. Recite this three or seven times.
Place it upon the crown of the head and scatter [the flowers].
By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra,
one awakens all the Buddhas of the Buddha Family.
May all of you assemble to empower and protect those who practice the true mantras,
swiftly causing them to attain purity of physical action,
the eradication of karmic obstacles, and the increase of merit and wisdom.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Lotus Family:
join the two hands with palms hollowed together;
interlace the tips of the two thumbs and the two little fingers respectively.
The remaining six fingers are slightly bent,
forming the shape of a blooming lotus flower;
thus it is accomplished.
Having bound this mudrā,
one should visualize the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with his marks and signs of excellence,
surrounded by an immeasurable koṭi of holy beings of the Lotus family.
Then recite the Samaya-mantra of the Padmakula as follows:
Oṃ vandanamo nābhavāya svāhā. Recite this three times or seven times.
Place the empowerment seal at the crown of the head and then release it.
By forming this seal and reciting the mantra,
one awakens Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and the holy assembly of the Lotus Family.
All of them come to empower the practitioner,
whereby one attains purity of vocal karma and a majestic,
solemn resonance.
This causes others to delight in hearing [the teaching] and attains unimpeded eloquence for preaching the Dharma with mastery.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Vajra Family:
with both hands, the left is inverted and the right is palm-upward.
Have them face each other with their backs touching.
Interlace the right thumb with the left little finger,
and interlace the left thumb with the right little finger.
Binding the middle six fingers around the wrists so that they form the shape of a three-pronged vajra,
it is thus completed.
Form the mudrā at the heart and visualize the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha with his auspicious marks and majestic radiance,
surrounded by an immeasurable retinue of Vajradharas.
Then, recite the Samaya-mantra of the Vajra Family:
Oṃ vairocana svāhā. Recite this three times or seven times.
Place the *an* mudrā at the crown of the head and then disperse it to the left.
By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra,
one awakens the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha and the assembly of deities of the Vajra family.
All shall come to empower the practitioner,
who will attain purity of mental action, realize the bodhicitta,
manifest samādhi, and swiftly achieve liberation.
Next, perform the Armor for Protecting the Body mudrā:
interlace the two little fingers and the two ring fingers with the right hand pressing over the left.
The two middle fingers are held straight upright with their tips touching one another;
the two index fingers are bent into the shape of hooks and placed against the backs of the middle fingers, ensuring they do not touch them.
Place the two thumbs side by side and upright, pressing against the ring fingers;
thus the mudrā is formed.
Place it at the heart and recite the mantra.
Recite [the mantra] once for each of the five places of the body.
First, seal the forehead;
next, the right shoulder.
Next, [place them] on the left shoulder,
the heart, and the throat;
these constitute the five locations.
Immediately giving rise to great compassion, one universally takes all sentient beings as the object of focus,
making the vow that they shall all be adorned with the armor of great compassion and swiftly be freed from all obstacles and difficulties.
Having realized the supreme, most excellent accomplishments of both the mundane and supramundane worlds,
and having contemplated thus,
one becomes clad in the vajra armor.
None of the māras will dare to create obstacles or hindrances.
The mantra for protecting the body is:
Oṃ vajragīti pratyāhāraya svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [one is protected].
By the power of their compassionate heart and mindful concern,
all celestial Māras and various obstructors perceive the practitioner’s majestic radiance as brilliantly blazing like the orb of the sun.
Each gives rise to a mind of loving-kindness that cannot be obstructed;
even wicked people find no opportunity to cause harm;
and the afflictions, karma, and obstacles do not defile the body.
Furthermore, it protects against the sufferings of the evil realms in the future and leads to the swift realization of unsurpassed bodhi.
Next, form the mudrā of the vajra-kila for the boundary of the earth.
First, insert the right middle finger between the left head-finger and the middle finger;
then insert the right ring finger between the left ring finger and the little finger,
with both fingers protruding from the top.
Wrap the left middle finger around the back of the right middle finger and insert it between the tips of the right index fingers;
wrap the left ring finger around the back of the right ring finger.
Insert [the right thumb] between the ring fingers;
join the tips of the two ring fingers with the tips of the two index fingers,
and press the undersides of the two thumbs together.
It is accomplished immediately.
Having bound this mudrā,
visualize the mudrā as having the shape of a vajra.
Touch the ground with the two thumbs;
recite the mantra once and perform the mudrā on the ground once.
Do this three times.
It immediately becomes a firm adamantine seat.
The mantra for the lower part is:
Oṃ kili kili vajravajri pūraya pūraya hūṃ phaṭ. By the power of binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra with empowerment, [the ground is stabilized].
Extending downward to the limit of the vajra-circle,
it forms an indestructible vajra realm that even the most powerful māras cannot shake.
With little exertion of effort, one attains great accomplishment;
all the foul and impure things within the earth are entirely purified through the power of empowerment.
That boundary is established according to the size of one's intention.
Next, perform the mudrā of the Vajra Wall,
following the previous mudrā for the Earth Boundary.
Open the palms and extend the two thumbs upright;
when they form the shape of a wall, it is accomplished.
Visualize blazing flames streaming forth from the mudrā.
Rotate the mudrā clockwise three times around the body while reciting the aforementioned earth-element mantra;
this immediately forms a vajra fortress of adamantine solidity.
The mantra for the boundary of the wall is:
Oṃ sara sara vajraprākāra hūṃ phaṭ. By means of binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra through the power of visualization, [the boundary is established].
According to the size of one's mind,
it forms a square boundary wall of vajra light-flames;
all demons, evil persons, tigers, wolves, and lions [are thereby warded off].
Furthermore, various venomous insects will be unable to approach.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Mahā-ākāśagarbha:
join the two hands in *añjali*.
Interlace the two middle fingers with the right over the left,
binding them across the backs of the hands;
then, press the two index fingers together so that they form the shape of a jewel.
It is accomplished immediately.
Visualize that from the mudrā flow forth immeasurable articles of offering— robes, food, drink, palaces, pavilions, and so forth—
as extensively described in the *Yogatantra*.
Then he recited the mantra of the Bodhisattva Mahā-ākāśagarbha, saying:
*Oṃ ākāśasambhava vajra hūṃ*. Even if the power of the practitioner’s contemplation and visualization is weak, [the mantra shall prevail].
By virtue of the empowering power of this mudrā and mantra,
all offering substances become truly real,
just as when one performs vast offerings within the world of Sukhāvatī.
Next, visualize within the maṇḍala the syllable *hrīḥ*,
which emits great rays of light, the color of red crystal,
illuminating the worlds of the ten directions.
Among those sentient beings who encounter this light,
there are none whose karmic obstructions are not completely eliminated.
Next, form the Tathāgata Fist Mudrā.
Form a fist with the four fingers of the left hand and extend the thumb straight upward;
form a vajra-fist with the right hand.
Grasp the left thumb;
this completes it.
With this fist-seal, seal the ground.
Recite the mantra seven times to empower it,
thereby transforming that world.
The Tathāgata-muṣṭi (Buddha-fist) mantra is as follows:
Oṃ bhu jaḥ khaṃ. By the power of binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra, this trichiliocosm was immediately transformed.
He shall establish the Land of Ultimate Bliss,
with the seven treasures as its ground;
where the water-birds and the forest trees all proclaim the sounds of the Dharma.
The immeasurable adornments are as described in the sutra;
one then recites the verse:
By the power of my merit, And by the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment...
And by the power of the dharma-realm, may the land of peace and bliss be realized;
for as the practitioner repeatedly cultivates this samādhi,
in every present life they dwell within it during meditative concentration.
They behold the Tathāgata Amitāyus in the world of Sukhāvatī amidst an assembly of great bodhisattvas,
and hear him preach immeasurable sūtras;
at the time of their death, their minds remain undisturbed.
When samādhi manifests before them,
they will be born in that land with instantaneous swiftness. There,
they will be born transformationally from lotus flowers and realize the stage of a bodhisattva.
Next, form the seal of the precious chariot:
with both hands turned upward and interlaced,
let the right hand press down upon the left.
Place the two index fingers side by side, touching each other,
and press the two thumbs against the first joint below the two index fingers;
thus it is formed.
The mantra for the vehicle is: Oṃ tulu tulu hūṃ yojaya.
Form this mudrā and visualize it as a carriage adorned with the seven precious jewels.
Proceed to that world of Ultimate Bliss and invite the Tathāgata Amitāyus, along with his retinue of bodhisattvas, to mount this carriage;
do not disperse this seal.
With the two thumbs directed toward the body,
flick the tips of the two middle fingers,
and then recite the *ratha-mantra* as follows:
*Namo viśuddhivikaraṇa-tathāgatāya. Oṃ vairocanīyanakarasaye svāhā.* Then, visualize that the celestial chariot arrives at the site of practice and abides in the midst of space.
Next, perform the mudrā for inviting the assembly of noble ones:
with both hands, place the right over the left and interlace the fingers inwardly,
then form fists.
Cause the palms to touch.
Bend the left thumb into the palm;
curve the right thumb like a hook.
One beckons it toward oneself.
Then, one recites the invocation mantra, saying:
*Oṃ āluḥ khāhi svāhā*. Because this seal is bound and the mantra is recited to perform the invitation, [the deity is summoned].
The Tathāgata Amitāyus, not forsaking his compassionate vows,
proceeded to this site of the pure land bodhimaṇḍa produced by this samādhi,
together with a multitude of immeasurable koṭis of great bodhisattvas.
The practitioner who receives these offerings will swiftly attain the supreme accomplishment (*uttarottara-siddhi*).
Next, bind the mudrā of Avalokiteśvara Hayagrīva.
To perform the ritual of warding off obstacles and establishing the boundary (*sīmābandha*), join the two hands in *añjali*.
The two index fingers and the two ring fingers are bent into the palms with their respective backs facing one another;
both thumbs are slightly bent.
Do not touch the tip of the index finger;
it is then accomplished.
Recite the mantra of Hayagrīva as follows:
Recite "Oṃ amṛtodbhava hūṃ phaṭ svāhā" three times.
Then, rotate the mudrā to the left three times.
All māras are expelled and naturally disperse;
by rotating the seal three times to the right,
a firm and great boundary is immediately established.
Next, form the Vajrapāśa mudrā.
Following the previous earth-boundary mudrā,
join the two thumbs.
Pressing the first joint of the two index fingers,
it is thus formed.
Recite the mantra three times.
Recite [the mantra] while sealing the crown of the head with a clockwise rotation and then releasing the mudrā.
The Net-Boundary (Jālaparigha) mantra is:
Oṃ viśvapara-nara-kṣa-vajra-panjara hūṃ phaṭ. By the power of binding this seal and reciting this mantra for consecration, [the boundary is established].
Immediately above,
it was covered with a net of adamantine solidity,
such that even the gods of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations could not transgress it or create obstacles.
The practitioner’s body and mind will be peaceful and blissful,
and samādhi will be easily attained and accomplished.
Next, form the mudrā of the Vajra Fire Court Boundary.
Cover the back of the right hand with the palm of the left hand so that they touch;
extend both thumbs upright, and it is thus completed.
Visualize immeasurable flames of light streaming forth from the mudrā.
Rotate the fire clockwise three times with the mudrā;
then, outside the vajra wall,
flames will immediately surround it.
This immediately establishes the great boundary (*mahā-sīmā*) of the firm and pure fire-court (*agni-koṭa*).
The mantra of the fire-court is:
Oṃ āsamayiṇi hūṃ phaṭ. Next, one should form the mudrā for offering the *argha* perfumed water.
Holding the arghya vessel with both hands,
offer it at the forehead and recite the mantra three times.
Visualize bathing the feet of the assembly of noble ones.
The *argha* mantra is as follows:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ gaganasamavasaraṇāya svāhā*. By offering this *argha* perfumed water, one performs the ritual worship.
It causes the practitioner’s three karmas to be purified,
washing away all afflictions and the defilements of sin,
from the stage of practice through resolute belief.
Upon reaching the tenth stage and the stage of the Tathāgata,
when one realizes the pāramitās of these stages,
one receives the empowerment of the nectar-like Dharma-water of all Tathāgatas.
Next, form the Flower Seat Mudrā.
It is the same as the previous Samaya Mudrā of the Lotus Family;
simply slightly bend the index fingers to make them rounded, and that is it.
Having bound this mudrā,
visualize that from it flow forth immeasurable vajra-lotuses,
which pervade this world of Sukhāvatī.
The Tathāgata Amitāyus, along with all the great Bodhisattvas and the entire assembly of holy ones,
each obtains this vajra-lotus as a seat.
The mantra of the lotus seat is as follows:
Oṃ kamala svāhā. By binding the lotus-seat mudrā and reciting this mantra to empower it, the practitioner attains the fulfillment of the ten stages (daśabhūmi) and shall obtain the vajra-seat.
The three karmas are as firm and solid as vajra.
Next, form the seal of the vast Amoghamani offering:
join the two hands in the vajra-palms gesture.
Curl the two index fingers into the shape of a jewel;
by simultaneously extending the two thumbs, the mudrā is formed.
Then recite the *Mahā-amogha-maṇi-pūjā-dhāraṇī*:
Oṃ amoghapūjāmaṇipadmaratne tathāgatavilocite samantaprabhasara hūṃ. This is the extensive Amoghamani-pūjā-dhāraṇī.
Upon reciting it three times,
one immediately brings about the assembly of the Tathāgata Amitāyus and causes an immeasurable rain of vast offerings to fall throughout as many lands as there are atoms.
That is to say: oceans of clouds of various kinds of unguents;
oceans of clouds of various kinds of flower garlands;
and oceans of clouds of various kinds of burning incense.
An ocean-like cloud of various kinds of exquisite celestial food and drink;
an ocean-like cloud of various kinds of exquisite celestial garments;
and an ocean-like cloud of the radiant light of various kinds of mani-jewel lamps and candles.
Cloud-oceans of various banners, pennants, precious canopies, and jeweled parasols;
cloud-oceans of various sublime celestial music;
[all] throughout the assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
This constitutes a truly vast and authentic offering;
by forming mudrās and making offerings while reciting this mantra,
one obtains an immeasurable accumulation of merit.
Like space, it is without limit;
in every lifetime, one is constantly born within the great assemblies of all Tathāgatas,
arising by transformation from a lotus and attaining the five supernormal powers.
Manifesting ten billion emanation bodies,
he is able to rescue and deliver suffering sentient beings within defiled worlds.
All shall be at peace and find benefit;
they will receive immeasurable karmic rewards in this very life and,
in the future, attain rebirth in a pure land.
Next, one should clarify the mind and stabilize the intention, focusing single-mindedly on a single object.
One should contemplate the Tathāgata Amitāyus until he is perceived with perfect clarity, as if standing before one's eyes.
Possessing all the primary and secondary marks,
together with immeasurable retinues and those buddha-fields,
they aspire to them with joy at every thought-moment.
Having attained the accomplishment of samādhi before one’s eyes,
one should with sincere single-mindedness aspire to be born in that land,
maintaining an uninterrupted continuity of thought without allowing the mind to wander to other objects.
Then, recite the Praise to the Tathāgata Amitāyus three times.
The praise says:
*Namo 'mitābhāya*, *namo 'mitāyūṣe*. *Namaḥ...* [The text continues with the invocation.]
Namaḥ jinatraya-ghuṇḍakāra-damane | Namaḥ mitābhāya īrṇyate munisukhavati jñānītavānubhijñāpāya sukha-vati ||
*Gargaṇaka-vicitraka-nānām amaro-maṃ sugata-sudāra-laṅkṛta-dhṛddhaṃ dīva-śiriyā-datta-pratītya-guṇa-śrī-mate.*
8. *prajñāmiṣṭam āhuḥ kulaniruttara-tantrasañcayaṃ* 9.
The practitioner, at the three periods of each day...
Constantly reciting this praise of the Buddha’s merits awakens the Tathāgata Amitāyus,
who does not abandon his compassionate vows.
Immeasurable light shines upon and touches the practitioner,
whereby all heavy karmic obstructions and grave offenses are completely extinguished;
body and mind become peaceful, blissful, serene, and joyful.
Sitting for a long time in recitation without becoming weary,
one’s mind attains purity and swiftly realizes samādhi;
one immediately enters the samādhi of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Close your eyes and clarify the mind.
Visualize within your own body a perfect, pure white form,
like the bright moon gazing upward within the heart.
Upon the pure moon,
one visualizes the syllable *dhrīṃ* emitting great light;
that syllable transforms into an eight-petaled lotus flower.
Upon the lotus flower is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
with his marks and signs clearly distinct;
his left hand holds a lotus flower.
With his right hand, he makes the gesture of opening a blooming leaf.
This Bodhisattva then reflects:
"Within the bodies of all sentient beings..."
Possessing this awakening-lotus,
the pure dharmadhātu is unstained by afflictions;
upon its eight petals, [the following resides].
In each [lotus] sits a Tathāgata in meditative absorption, seated in the full lotus posture,
facing the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
with a halo encircling his neck.
One's body is golden in color, radiating brilliant light.
Then one visualizes this eight-petaled lotus flower,
which gradually expands and increases in size until it is equal to empty space.
He then formed this thought:
"May these *bodhi*-flowers, by their illuminating touch, reach the ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata,
and may they become a vast and magnificent offering."
If the mind does not shift from this meditative concentration,
one then gives rise to profound compassion for infinite sentient beings;
those who are touched and illuminated by these flowers of awakening—
Being completely liberated from all suffering and afflictions,
one becomes equal to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara; then,
one should visualize the lotus gradually contracting until its size is equal to one's own body.
Then, one should form the mudrā of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and empower the four places:
namely, the heart, the forehead, the throat, and the crown of the head.
To form this mudrā, interlace the two hands with the palms facing outward.
Support the two index fingers against each other like lotus petals;
when the two thumbs are held upright side by side, it is accomplished.
Then he recited the mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva:
Oṃ vajradharma hrīḥ jūḥ. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra, he performed the empowerment.
One should then visualize oneself as identical to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
without any difference whatsoever.
Next, one binds the fundamental mudrā of the Tathāgata Amitāyus.
Interlace the two hands externally;
form fists and extend the tips of the two middle fingers so that they touch,
forming the shape of a lotus petal.
Having formed the mudrā,
recite the dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata Amitāyus seven times,
and then release the mudrā over the crown of the head.
The Root Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata Amitāyus is as follows:
Namo ratnatrayāya | Namo ’rhatvabhisaṃbuddhāya | Tathāgatāya arhate ||
ṛddhāve 8 amṛta-siddhe 9 amṛtadevi 10 amṛtavikrīḍite 11 amṛtavikrīḍitagarmini 12.
12. amṛtagaganagatike | 13. amṛtanaṃnubhi svāhe | 14.
sarvārthasādhanī | 15. sarvakarmakleśa-kṣayaṃ kuru ||
*Sāṃkhye svāhā*. This dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata Amitāyus,
by reciting it even once, [brings about its effect].
Thereby, the ten unwholesome actions, the four grave offenses, and the five crimes of immediate retribution within one's body are extinguished;
all karmic obstructions are entirely eliminated.
This applies even if a bhikṣu or bhikṣuṇī has committed a root offense.
Having recited it seven times,
one immediately regains the purity of the precepts;
if one recites it ten thousand times, [the same result is attained].
One attains the samādhi of the non-forgetfulness of bodhicitta;
bodhicitta manifests within the body,
pure, radiant, and perfectly luminous like the bright moon.
At the time of death,
one will see the Tathāgata Amitāyus surrounded by a retinue of immeasurable koṭis of bodhisattvas coming to welcome the practitioner.
With body and mind thus comforted, one is immediately reborn in the World of Ultimate Bliss in the highest grade of the highest birth,
attaining the rank of a Bodhisattva;
one then takes up a lotus-seed rosary.
Resting it in the palms of the hands,
the two hands hold the jewel with palms joined in the shape of an unfurled lotus flower.
Consecrate the thousand-turn rosary seven times with the mantra. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajrayakṣiṇī-jāpamaye hūṃ. Having performed the consecration, [proceed].
He then took up the jewel, placed it upon his head,
and made this aspiration: "May all sentient beings swiftly accomplish their supreme worldly and supramundane aspirations."
Then, place both hands at the heart; with each hand,
cup the five fingers together like an unopened lotus flower,
and hold the rosary with the left hand.
With the thumb and forefinger of the right hand,
move the beads while reciting the dhāraṇī once,
accompanied by the sound of the syllable *svāhā*.
Shift one bead at a time.
The sound of recitation should be neither slow nor fast, neither high nor low;
it should not be audible.
Recite the mantra syllables, making each one distinct and clear.
With the mind, visualize this pure land produced by samādhi,
as well as the Amitāyus Buddha who was previously invited.
The [deity] with the marks and signs of perfection resides within the maṇḍala.
Visualize this practice clearly and distinctly in this manner,
reciting with focused concentration without interruption.
Remaining free from distraction,
one should recite the mantra while seated either a hundred or a thousand times;
if one does not complete one hundred and eight recitations, [the practice is incomplete].
Thus, one need not fulfill the required number of recitations;
by virtue of the empowerment of the Tathāgata Amitāyus,
one’s body and mind become pure.
Even until the opening and closing of their eyes,
they constantly see the Tathāgata Amitāyus;
within that very meditative concentration, they hear the preaching of the profound and wondrous Dharma.
In each and every syllable and each and every phrase,
one awakens to immeasurable gates of samādhi, immeasurable gates of dhāraṇī, and immeasurable gates of liberation;
this body becomes identical to that of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
One will swiftly reach that land.
When the recitation count is completed,
hold the rosary in one's hands, place it upon the crown of the head, and make this vow:
May all sentient beings be reborn in the world of Ultimate Bliss,
where they may behold the Buddha and hear the Dharma.
May one swiftly realize unsurpassed bodhi.
Next, form the seal of concentration (*samādhi-mudrā*) and visualize the bodhicitta within one's own body.
It is pure, bright, and perfectly luminous, like the full moon.
Furthermore, one should reflect:
"The essence of bodhicitta is free from all things."
Because there are no aggregates, elements, or sense-bases, and because it is free from the grasper and the grasped,
phenomena are of one mark and equal due to the selflessness of dharmas;
for the mind is fundamentally unarisen, and being empty of intrinsic nature, its very nature is emptiness.
Then, upon a perfectly pure lunar disc,
one should visualize the syllable-hinge *hrīḥ*.
From this syllable, immeasurable rays of light stream forth.
Within each path of light,
one visualizes the accomplishment of the world of Ultimate Bliss,
with the Holy Assembly surrounding Amitāyus Buddha, as described in the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*.
Having thus performed the recitation and cultivated samādhi,
when one wishes to exit the maṇḍala,
one should immediately form the mudrā of the deity.
Recite the root dhāraṇī seven times,
scatter it over the crown of the head with the mudrā,
and then recite the mantra of praise.
Having completed the praise and mantra,
next form the seal of universal offering and recite the *Vistara-Amogha-mani-pūjā-dhāraṇī*.
Again, offer argha water and declare all the aspirations held in your heart to the assembly of noble ones:
"I pray only that the Noble Ones will not transgress their original vows and fulfill my wishes."
Having thus performed the recitation, offerings, and made the aspiration,
one should immediately form the previously mentioned seal of the fire enclosure (*agnimaṇḍala*),
rotate it once counter-clockwise, and dissolve the previously established boundary.
Next, bind the seal of the precious chariot:
extend the two thumbs outward and push the tips of the two middle fingers apart.
Recite the root mantra to respectfully dismiss the assembly of noble beings.
Next, bind the samaya-mudrās of the three families and recite their respective mantras three times each.
Thereafter, perform the armor-binding seal to protect the body,
sealing the five locations of the body,
and then stand before the Principal Deity.
With sincere devotion, make vows and pay homage to the Buddha;
then, as you please, leave the ritual enclosure and practice walking meditation at will.
You should constantly recite the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*.
Do not harbor conceit; instead, apply yourself with diligence to recitation,
seal the Buddha-seal upon stupas, take pleasure in performing mandala offerings,
and cultivate the observance of precepts, patience, vigor, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
All the virtuous qualities they have cultivated are dedicated toward rebirth in the Pure Land together with all sentient beings, attaining the highest grade of the highest birth.
Therein they realize the Stage of Joy and receive the prediction of unsurpassed bodhi.
The Heart Mantra of the Tathāgata Amitāyus:
Oṃ lokeshvara rāja kṛi. Recite this mantra once.
The enemy recites the *Amitābha Sūtra* but once, while this [mantra] is unspeakable times;
because it is secret and supreme, its power to shatter heavy obstructions and difficulties cannot be fully described.
Oṃ amṛtatejorāja hūṃ. This dharma is common to all the Lotus Family: the Recitation Method of the Tathāgata Amitāyus.
Upon completing one hundred thousand recitations,
one shall behold Amitābha Tathāgata;
at the end of life, one will certainly attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

The *Dhāraṇī of the Vow of the Tathāgata Amitāyus*, *Kārikā-śa-kāritā-niyā-nirukti*: 1. *Māyinindatodū* 2. *Vimucyantu ruka* 3. *Mama ca sucarite* 4. *Namaḥ sarvabuddhapramukhebhyaḥ* 5. *Sukhavati-prayāntu* The Ritual for the Contemplative Practice and Offering to the Tathāgata Amitāyus.
